name: Legacy, non-MFA compatible authentication protocols (e.g., POP3, IMAP, SMTP) MUST be explicitly disabled because they eliminate easy ways for hackers to bypass strong MFA.
conditionsText: Any service that uses older authentication methods and do not support MFA
requirementTitle: Legacy, non-MFA compatible authentication protocols (e.g., POP3, IMAP, SMTP) MUST be explicitly disabled because they eliminate easy ways for hackers to bypass strong MFA.
requirementDescription: Older authentication methods that do not support Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) must be turned off so attackers cannot use them to avoid MFA protections.
why:
- Passwords are frequently stolen through phishing attacks.
- MFA is one of the most effective defences against account compromise.
- Legacy protocols can undermine MFA.
- Attackers specifically target old authentication methods because they are easier to exploit.
